title: Federal Register: Calendar Year 2027 Home Health Prospective Payment System Rate Update; HH Quality Reporting Program (CMS-1844-P), proposed rule

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (via GovInfo / Federal Register)
source_type: Government proposed rule with regulatory flexibility analysis and information collection section
reliability: Government document; the issuing agency (CMS) is also the party imposing and administering the requirement. Proposed rule; content may change in a final rule that was not read.
findings: CMS states that approximately 96 percent of HHAs are considered small entities (NAICS 621610, size standard $19 million).
CMS proposes to revise HH QRP data submission deadlines and the OASIS annual payment update reporting timeframe; it states the net effect is no change in burden for OASIS data collection.

Using 2024 data, CMS reports 99.27 percent of all OASIS assessments were submitted to CMS within a 45-day timeframe; it states only 0.49 percent of assessments would be affected by moving the deadline from 4.5 months to the 15th day of the second month after the quarter.
CMS notes that failure to submit OASIS data timely results in a 2 percentage point reduction of the annual home health market basket increase for the corresponding calendar year.
CMS reports a CY 2025 RFI on shortening the OASIS submission deadline from 4.5 months to 45 days, with comments summarized in the CY 2026 final rule (which was not read).

CMS concludes the payment policies would have a significant positive economic impact on a substantial number of small entities (net estimated +2.4 percent, about $420 million, in the aggregate for CY 2027).
limitations: Proposed rule dated July 6, 2026; whether it was finalized, and with what changes, was not checked.
Only the OASIS-related sections, the information collection section and the small-entity discussion were read, not the whole rule.
The OASIS burden statement is a "no change" statement relative to the existing approved collection; it does not itself quantify burden.
Table 39/40 data on small-firm revenue are graphics and were not extracted.
